sections.overview: Cirrhoscyllium formosanum is a small carpet shark recorded around Taiwan and regarded by Taiwanese sources as endemic to the island.
sections.identification: It has a slender body, throat barbels and dark crossbands; older Taiwanese records show that it has sometimes been confused with C. expolitum or C. japonicum.
sections.habitat: The Taiwan Fish Database records coastal and deeper benthic habitat, including a type locality off Kaohsiung at about 110 m; surveys also suggest occurrence near 200 m in the Kaoping Trench.
sections.diet: Species-specific prey have not been documented well enough in the sources consulted to describe its diet.
sections.behavior: It is a rarely recorded bottom-associated shark, and its habits remain little known.
sections.reproduction: The literature reports egg-laying for this species, but detailed timing and breeding sites are not established.
sections.ecology: It is the Taiwan-restricted member of a three-species genus; unlike C. expolitum from the South China Sea and C. japonicum recorded around Japan, its known records cluster around Taiwan.
sections.conservation: The IUCN global assessment categorizes it as Vulnerable; a Taiwanese database still shows Data Deficient, reflecting differences in assessment source or update.
